Replies.Text:
Design, Step 5: Title and Chrome. Twelve decisions, each with my recommendation first. Resolve with no reply to take them all; reply with the numbers you want otherwise, and I apply the result under "Decided before the build".

1. The components. Two: title-bar (the bar: the brand, the application menu button, the status, the look button; the drag region in the desktop) and look-controls (the theme, size and editor selects, as they are in the sidebar's bottom today, in a popover the look button opens). sidebar.js and its SidebarController go: the aside holds <project-tree> alone. help.js keeps HelpController for the About and Hotkeys popups; the Help menu button goes, its two items move into the application menu. Alternative: a third component, app-status, for the counts; I would not, the status is two links.

2. Where the bar sits. <title-bar> is the first thing in the body, above .layout; the body becomes a flex column and .layout takes the rest (its height: 100vh becomes flex: 1 with min-height: 0). The bar is the same in the main window, a detached window (brand, menu and status; no tree, as now) and a browser. The popup menu, the Help and Settings popups and the toast stay where they are.

3. The desktop window. Both the main window and the detached windows (the window-open handler's options) take titleBarStyle "hidden" with titleBarOverlay, so Electron draws minimize, maximize and close over the bar's right end; nothing else of the frame remains. The bar is -webkit-app-region: drag, its buttons and links no-drag; a double-click on it maximizes, as the frame did. The bar sits at env(titlebar-area-x) and is env(titlebar-area-width) wide, with 0 and 100% as the fallbacks, so a browser gets the full width and a macOS window would leave the traffic lights their corner.

4. The overlay's colours and height. main.js opens the window with a light or a dark pair from the settings' theme (the palette's exact colours are the page's); once the page renders, and after every theme or size change, the page sends the bar's computed background, text colour and height over a new bridge call, ConsensusDesktop.SetChrome( { Color, Symbol, Height } ), and main.js calls setTitleBarOverlay on the sender's window. So the buttons match the palette and the bar's height follows the size setting (the bar is sized in rem). The connect screen does the same from its header, which becomes the drag region there (its title and its two selects as they are), or the servers screen could not be moved.

5. The native menu. The menu bar is no longer shown (the hidden frame has none, and setMenuBarVisibility( false ) keeps Alt from bringing it back), but the Menu is still built and set, since its accelerators are what keep Ctrl+R, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Shift+O, F12 and Ctrl+Shift+I (DevTools), Ctrl+0, Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- (zoom) and F11 (full screen) working. The View menu's items appear in no visible menu: they stay keys. Alternative: new IPC for each so the application menu lists them; not worth it for the developer tools and the zoom.

6. The application menu. One button in the bar after the brand, labelled Menu with the caret icon, id app-menu, opening the Menus popup (the one the tree and the tabs use). Items: About, Hotkeys; then, when window.Desktop is there, a separator and Servers…, New window, Open folder in new window…, Reload, a separator and Quit. Servers… and New window call the bridge as the tree does today; Open folder in new window and Quit are two new bridge calls (OpenFolderWindow and Quit; main.js has the functions). Reload is the page's own location.reload(), no bridge. "The page" goes: the page is where the menu is. The root rows' menus keep Servers… and Reload (a root's reload re-reads that server, a different thing), New Project, Import and Settings.

7. The status. At the bar's right, before the look button: "Waiting on you: N", the link it is today (id waiting-link, to #/waiting, marked open on that view), counted over every root as now; and "Running: N" only while N > 0, counted over every root's Llms.For( root ).Running, a link to the first running run's LLM page (#/s/<root>#/llm/<id>), its tooltip naming every running connection and its server. The count follows runs-changed, which the Llms service already broadcasts.

8. The look button. A gear button at the bar's far right (id look-button) opens a popover under it holding look-controls: the three selects with the ids they have (theme-select, scale-select, editor-select) and their labels Theme, Size, Editor beside them. A click outside or Escape closes it, as the menu closes. Alternative: the three selects in the bar itself; too much for a title bar, and they wrap at a narrow width.

9. Styles. .sidebar-top, .brand, .menu-bar, .menu-bar-item, .waiting-link, .sidebar-bottom and .theme-controls leave consensus.css for title-bar.css and look-controls.css (renamed where the class goes: the bar's button is .title-button). The bar: the panel background, a bottom border, 2.25rem high at the normal size, the brand at 1.1rem as now. The help popups' rules (.help-form) stay in consensus.css with the popups.

10. The page title. The bar shows the brand only; the open item is named in its tab and the header, and the window's own title stays "Consensus Desktop" for the task bar. Alternative: the open item's title in the bar's middle; it would repeat the tab.

11. Tests. The Help test picks About and Hotkeys from #app-menu; the editor tests open the look popover before reaching #editor-select; the waiting-link test holds as it is. New browser tests: the bar renders with the brand, the menu, the waiting link and the look button; the menu in a browser has the two items and no desktop items; the look popover opens, changes the theme, and closes on Escape. Desktop.test.js stays without Electron. The build also runs one Electron smoke on a temporary config (--config, --port 0) and its own --user-data-dir, over DevTools: the window opens without a frame, the overlay takes the palette's colours after a theme change, the menu lists the desktop items, Open folder in new window and Quit are wired; screenshots of the bar in light and dark. Nothing of the real desktop.json is touched.

12. Out of this step. The guide's getting-started page describes the Server menu and the sidebar's controls; Step 6 rewrites it with the pictures. The Hotkeys popup does not list the desktop's keys; it could in Step 6.

Applied.Outcome: The build was accepted as reported; no text change. Committed as "UI Components: Step 5".

Replies.Text:
Build log, Step 5: Title and Chrome. Built by Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1) through the Claude Code CLI, as the twelve decisions say. Not committed yet: resolve to accept, and I commit it as "UI Components: Step 5".

What was built, and where:
- public/components/title-bar: the bar across the top of the page: the brand, the Menu button (About and Hotkeys; in the desktop also Servers…, New window, Open folder in new window…, Reload and Quit, over the bridge), the status (Waiting on you over every root, to the Waiting view; Running while a run is in progress on any root, to the first running run's LLM page, its tooltip naming every running connection and its server) and the gear button whose popover holds look-controls. In the desktop it is the drag region and reports its colours and height once drawn and after every change of theme or size.
- public/components/look-controls: the theme, size and editor selects, a label beside each, under the ids they had.
- public/js/help.js: the About summary and the opening moved into the HelpPanel service (Show, Close), so the menu could leave; HelpController keeps the two popups. sidebar.js and SidebarController are gone; the aside holds <project-tree> alone.
- public/index.html: <title-bar> first in the body, above the layout; the body is a flex column and the layout takes the rest. The shell's rules (sidebar-top, brand, menu-bar, waiting-link, sidebar-bottom, theme-controls) left consensus.css (870 lines) for the two stylesheets.
- public/js/theme.js: ReportChrome( element ) measures an element's background, text colour and height and sends them over ConsensusDesktop.SetChrome when the desktop is the host; the title bar and the connect screen call it.
- desktop/main.js: every window (the main one and the detached ones) opens with titleBarStyle hidden and titleBarOverlay, a light or dark pair first, the page's colours after; the menu bar is hidden on every window and the menu stays set for its accelerators; new handlers for the chrome message (setTitleBarOverlay on the sender's window, the colours and height checked), Open folder in new window and Quit. desktop/preload.js: SetChrome, OpenFolderWindow, Quit.
- desktop/page/connect.css and connect.js: the header is the drag region, its two selects stop short of the window buttons, and it reports its chrome as the page does.

Decided during the build:
1. The colour measuring lives in theme.js as ReportChrome rather than in the component, since the connect screen (its own small page) needs the same thing; both pages load theme.js.
2. The host element of title-bar spans the window and carries the colours; the bar inside is the titlebar-area wide, so the room under the window buttons has the same background.
3. The look popover closes on its button again as well as on a click elsewhere or Escape; the browser test's helper uses the button, since Escape also deselects the selected thread when no popup is open (the Hotkeys service's rule, unchanged).
4. The desktop items of the menu that need the new bridge calls (Open folder in new window, Quit) appear only when those calls exist, so the page shows nothing it cannot do against an older preload.
5. The chrome message takes a colour only as #rrggbb and a height only between 24 and 96 pixels, and a failed setTitleBarOverlay is logged, not thrown.

How it was tested:
- npm test: 187 tests pass (one new browser test: the bar renders with its parts and nothing of the shell is left in the sidebar; the menu in a browser has About and Hotkeys and no desktop items; the look popover opens with the three selects, a theme picked applies, Escape closes it). The Help test picks from #app-menu; the CodeMirror test sets the editor through the popover.
- A browser probe over a temporary server with a copy of the Consensus project: the layout ends at the window's bottom with no page scroll, the bar grows with the large size, the Waiting view marks its link, no console errors; screenshots light and dark.
- An Electron smoke on a temporary config (--config, --port 0) and its own --user-data-dir, over DevTools, 20 checks: the window controls overlay is visible and its area stops before the buttons; the bar is exactly that wide, is the drag region, its buttons are not; the overlay's height matches the bar and follows the large size; no frame above the page; the menu lists About, Hotkeys, Servers…, New window, Open folder in new window…, Reload and Quit; the three bridge calls exist; a detached window has the same bar and no frame; the connect screen's header is the drag region, its controls stop before the buttons, the overlay follows its height; Quit ends the app. Whole-window screen captures in light and dark show the buttons in the palette's colours. The real desktop.json was not touched.

Noted: your desktop on port 3500 stopped during this build, between my checkpoint 1 probe and the smoke's first run (the test suite and the smoke's own Electron instance ran in that window; the smoke's Quit went to its own instance over its own DevTools port). I did not restart it.

Not in this step: the guide's text on the Server menu and the sidebar's controls, and the desktop's keys in the Hotkeys popup (Step 6).
